turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Price section didn't work. Too many numbers at too many sizes. Couldn't spot the total without reading every label."

We want to understand what you meant by "couldn't spot the total without reading every label", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The lack of visual hierarchy between the individual item prices and the final "Total" amount.
B) The proximity of the "Subtotal" and "Shipping" labels to the final "Total" figure.
C) The inconsistent font sizes used for different numerical values in the Order Summary section.
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What specific visual elements in the "Order Summary" section make it difficult for you to distinguish the final total from the individual item prices?
turns.a: Price breakdown. Multiple numbers, multiple sizes. Didn't read as a group. Couldn't immediately tell which was the total.

turns.q: If a developer built this layout exactly as shown, how would that impact someone trying to quickly confirm their final cost for the first time?
turns.a: Too many numbers at once. Couldn't tell which to look at first. Had to read each one.

turns.q: What would the correct version of that price section actually look like to make the total stand out immediately?
turns.a: Nearly moved on without confirming the total. Too many sizes at similar weights — couldn't tell which was the main one. Stopped and read each label to confirm.

turns.q: What would need to be reorganized in this layout for the distinction between individual items and the final total to be clear at a glance?
turns.a: Total needs to be the largest number in the section — obviously so. Line items all the same size, clearly smaller. Secondary text smaller still. That's a typographic scale. Right now there are five sizes in that section. There should be three.
